audit.study: Angrist & Lavy (2009), 'The Effects of High Stakes High School Achievement Awards: Evidence from a Randomized Trial', American Economic Review 99(4):1384-1414
audit.osf_reproduction_node: 563d4 (https://osf.io/563d4) SCORE Push-Button Reproduction RR ID 65996; data node xjwa6 (raw data); code node 5k36r. NOTE: task hint 'osf.io/jvwtb' is a FILE GUID (Transparency Trail docx) inside node 563d4 - resolved to real reproduction node 563d4 via OSF API v2
primary_sources: base99/00/01/02.dta + base_ns.sas7bdat (authors' raw data, OSF xjwa6, prepared by Yannay Spitzer 2008)
Human PBR outputs: t2_levels_estimates_NDM.dta, t4_levels_estimates_halves_NDM.dta, angrist_sas_ols.docx, logs

headline_claims.claim: The Achievement Awards program increased girls' 2001 Bagrut certification rates; OLS with full controls (school covariates, quartile dummies, micro covariates) coefficient = 0.105 with BRL standard error 0.047.
headline_claims.recomputed: coefficient 0.1047457; BRL SE 0.0472902 (independent port of brl.ado) - exact match

headline_claims.claim: The Award program had no effect on boys (OLS -0.022, logit -0.023 with full controls).
Girls in the top half of the lagged-score distribution: effect 0.206 (SE 0.079) - output driven by marginal students.
headline_claims.recomputed: logit marginal effect 0.2058262, N=933 - exact match (point estimate)

headline_claims.claim: Increased girls' matriculation translated into higher college attendance: top-quartile girls, all-academic OLS = 0.086 (SE 0.055).

recomputation.method: Independent Python (numpy/pandas/statsmodels/sas7bdat) re-derivation of every headline estimator from the authors' raw data, plus an independent port of the BRL (Bias-Reduced Linearization) cluster-variance routine from brl.ado
recomputation.table8: girls top-quartile college0 OLS 0.08545, robust SE 0.0557 (N=921)

independent_reproduction_vs_paper.point_estimates: ALL headline point estimates reproduce exactly at reported precision (Table 2 OLS & logit, Table 4 ME, Table 8 OLS).
independent_reproduction_vs_paper.flagship_se: BRL standard error 0.047 reproduced exactly (0.0472902) by independent implementation - the paper's most important inferential number.
independent_reproduction_vs_paper.supporting_se_magnitudes: HC1/robust cluster SEs consistent in magnitude (e.g., HC1 0.044 vs BRL 0.047; robust 0.0557 vs paper 0.055).

human_pbr_comparison: The SCORE human Push-Button Reproduction (RR 65996) reproduced all 5 focal claims precisely (girls OLS 0.105 -> 0.1047; girls logit 0.097 -> 0.0974; boys logit -0.023 -> -0.0234; Table 4 0.206 -> 0.2058; Table 8 0.086 -> 0.0855). This audit independently confirms each of those from the same raw data.

findings.title: Replication requires third-party 'brl' (Bias-Reduced Linearization) package not bundled in the paper's code
findings.detail: table-2.do errors ('command brl unrecognized') on stock Stata until brl.ado is installed from Frandsen's site. Package mirrored on OSF; analytically correct (BRL SE matches paper exactly). Friction only.

findings.title: Hard-coded absolute Windows working directories and output-erasing commands in analysis programs
findings.detail: do-files/SAS use cd 'W:\Student bonuses\...' and end with 'cap erase ..._estimates_NDM.dta' (erases primary outputs), requiring manual edits. No numerical impact.

grade_rationale: Data obtained (full raw dataset + code on OSF). Every headline numerical claim of this randomization-claims RCT was independently recomputed and matched exactly at the reported precision, including the flagship BRL standard error (0.047 -> 0.0472902) via an independent implementation. No P0/P1/P2 discrepancies. Only minor P3 reproducibility frictions exist, none touching results. This matches the human assessment that the code is computationally reproducible.
